text:
incident-bot: Pager: HIGH - automated alert: sustained 5xx spike from inference-proxy in us-west-3a (control plane and dataplane path errors). Impact: increased tail latency and request failures to hosted inference.
incident-bot: Metrics: 5xx rate ~6% over 3m, p95 latency 1.2s -> 2.8s, region us-west-3a. Suggested runbook: start failover policy, notify oncall.
mira (oncall): I'm on it. Acknowledging pager. Taking lead for mitigation.
sam (sre): Mira - can you confirm if it's ENI resets or control-plane mirrors? I see SYN retransmits from the proxy layer.
mira (oncall): Initial check: host-level network errors on a subset of GPU nodes. Netstat shows many TIME_WAIT and retransmits.
lee (infra): I'm pulling instance-level metrics now (ENIs, RX/TX drops). One AZ segment shows high TX errors on hosts in subnet sw3a-pool-13.
olivia (prod-eng): Quick customer impact check: dashboard shows ~12 active customers with elevated errors; two heavy-traffic tenants seeing 10-15% error rate. Dedicated customers appear OK (different AZ/placement).
nina (support): Can we draft a short customer message? ETA on mitigation?
zach (network): Correlating with cloud provider: I'm seeing sporadic link-level drops on the AZ's virtual network plane near 2026-02-18T15:04Z. Could be a noisy host or upstream ENI flaps.
mira (oncall): Action plan: 1) remove affected instances from LB rotation, 2) shift traffic to healthy AZs in region, 3) enable fallback to smaller model variants for latency-sensitive routes, 4) keep customers informed.
sam (sre): Agreed. Start with a targeted drain of instances in pool sw3a-pool-13. Use the drain script below to avoid losing inflight KV cache if possible:
```
/scripts/drain-instance --instance <id> --grace 30 --preserve-kv=true
```
mira (oncall): Running drain on i-0a3b2c... now. Marking in LB: out.
lee (infra): Executing NLB weight shift to other AZs, moving 40% traffic immediately. Command:
```
akctl traffic-shift --region us-west-3 --from az=us-west-3a --to az=us-west-3b --percent 40
```
olivia (prod-eng): Also toggling model-fallback for latency-sensitive endpoint (/v1/chat/low-latency) to model-compact-v2 for 5 minutes to reduce token compute latency. Patch rollout in progress.
incident-bot: Change request logged: CR-7892. Canary rollout 10% -> 100% in 5 min window.
nina (support): Draft for customers: "We’re experiencing increased errors and latency for inference requests in one AZ (us-west-3a). We’ve started routing traffic to healthy AZs and expect steady recovery in the next 15–30 minutes. We’ll follow up with a post-incident summary." Thoughts?
sam (sre): Good. Add that dedicated/reserved customers on private deployments are unaffected.
zach (network): Noted a retry storm pattern on the proxy level — some clients were aggressively retrying on 502 which amplified the issue. We're enabling a short client-side 429 backoff recommendation in the gateway to reduce retries.
mira (oncall): Applying gateway throttle rule:
```
/update-gateway-config --add retry-backoff=exponential --max-retries=2 --http-429-on-retry
```
lee (infra): After shifting + draining, p95 latency dropped to 1.1s, 5xx down to ~1.6% (3m). Good sign.
olivia (prod-eng): We also disabled cross-AZ KV cache replication for models being drained to avoid stale caches causing regen storms. Will re-enable after stabilization.
sam (sre): Could you paste the kube logs for the proxy pods that were killed? Any ENI detach events?
mira (oncall): Logs snippet: 
```
[proxy-logger] 15:06:31 WARNING connection reset by peer to 10.12.4.22:443
[proxy-logger] 15:06:33 ERROR downstream: write: broken pipe
[host] 15:06:35 kernel: rxtx errors on eth0: tx dropped count 512
```
zach (network): Cloud provider console shows instance-level network flaps and transient route table recursion on the switch for that host range. I've filed provider ticket with support case #AWSP-224511.
nina (support): Who will own customer comms now? I'll send the initial note and update after 30 min.
mira (oncall): Nina please send initial msg. Copy: "We’re routing traffic away from a subset of hardware in us-west-3a; mitigations in flight. We’ll provide updates at :30 and when fully restored."
nina (support): Sending now.
customer-comm-bot: Customer message posted to status.redwood.ai: "Partial degradation in us-west-3a affecting request latency & occasional failures. Engineering working on mitigation. No action required by customers at this time."
sam (sre): Remaining tasks: 1) continue draining affected hosts, 2) validate no KV cache thrash, 3) watch for retry amplification, 4) escalate to provider if new flaps.
lee (infra): I've queued replacement hosts for sw3a-pool-13 and will reprovision with fresh ENIs once provider confirms fabric health.
zach (network): Provider responded: suspected noisy NIC hardware causing route flap on hypervisor, they're evacuating the host group. ETA for fabric stabilization ~ 20–40 minutes.
mira (oncall): Monitoring. Current state: reduced errors, routing in progress. Keeping incident declared.
olivia (prod-eng): For long-term: we should add a circuit-breaker at the proxy for noisy-host detection and automatic per-host traffic quarantine to avoid regional retry storms. Filing infra story after incident.
sam (sre): Agreed. Also add autoscaling policy to bias cross-AZ capacity when a single-AZ exhibits >2% 5xx sustained.
nina (support): 30-minute update drafted and posted.
incident-bot: Severity: HIGH -> MONITORING (automated) - 5xx below threshold for 10m following traffic shift.
mira (oncall): Downgrading to monitoring but keeping oncall engaged until host evacuations complete. Will hand off in 1 hour unless symptoms recur.
sam (sre): Leaving a few watch scripts running:
```
/scripts/watch-metrics --region us-west-3 --metric 5xx_rate --threshold 2 --window 600
```
lee (infra): Replacement hosts spawned and healthy. Standing by to reintroduce once provider gives all-clear.
zach (network): Provider update: host evacuation done for target group, no further flaps observed in last 10m.
mira (oncall): Great. I'll prepare the post-incident notes and timeline. Nina, please include customer impact numbers (# affected tenants, max error rate, mitigation steps).
nina (support): Will do.
incident-bot: Incident closed (provisional) - will reopen if metrics regress.
